ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1820/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 09.12.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Kheda at Nadiad in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1133 of 2018, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.13,24,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimants, holding all the opponents liable,
jointly and severally.

sentences.text: There is no dispute raised with regard to the facts of the case nor about the negligence aspect has considered by the Tribunal and hence, that aspect requires no mention.

2. Mr. Nishit Bhalodi, learned advocate appearing for the appellants submits that the deceased was labourer aged about 37 years at the time of his death and he was maintaining his parents, wife and minor child.
The learned tribunal ought to have considered the minimum wages schedule keeping in mind the date of accident as 31.10.2018 and thus, has urged to consider the income accordingly.

Mr.
Bhalodi, learned advocate further submits that the learned tribunal has placed reliance on the judgment of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680, has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1820/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined considered 40% rise, which is consistent.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
And accordingly, submitted that the rest of the calculation is in accordance to the judgment of Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma (supra)
except the fact that the learned tribunal has cut down the monthly income.

3. Countering the argument, Mr. Tanmay Karia, learned advocate appearing for the Insurance Company has submitted that the assessment of income is in accordance to the facts and evidence,
while there is no corroborative evidence to suggest that the claimant was earning income even as per the minimum wages schedule.
4. The date of the accident was 31.10.2018.

The deceased was labourer, was maintaining his parents,
wife and minor child, keeping this fact in consideration, the minimum wages schedule is required to be made applicable and accordingly, the monthly income of Rs.8,118/- is assessed by this Court.

5. The learned tribunal has thereafter, given 40% rise in prospective income and 1/4th amount would be required to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1820/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023 undefined be deducted towards personal expenses considering the dependents, the multiplier 15 is rightly applied.
Thus, making it applicable to the minimum wages to Rs.8,118/-, the dependency loss would be Rs.11,365/- (Rs.8,118/- plus 40% rise).
The 1/4th amount is deducted against the personal expenses of the deceased, (Rs.11365/- minus Rs.2841/-)= Rs.8,524/-.

While considering the monthly income of Rs.8,524/- annually, which is multiplied for 12 months and by applying 15 Minaben Prahladbhai Solanki vs Dineshbhai Khetabhai Dama on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101775983/
2 multiplier, the dependency loss would come to Rs.15,34,320/-.

entities.text: Minaben Prahladbhai Solanki vs Dineshbhai Khetabhai Dama
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, amount of Rs.15,34,320/-
is awarded towards loss of dependency.

5. The learned tribunal has rightly considered the consortium amount, which is granted as Rs.1,60,000/-; loss of estate and funeral per head is Rs.1,5000/- and thus, in total Rs.30,000/-
granted, which required to be added to the compensation amount.

6. Therefore, the appellants - claimants are entitled to get the the following final amount as compensation:-
 Particulars

Amount (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 15,34,320/-

NEUTRAL CI  C/FA/1820/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/02/2023  undefined  Consortium 1,60,000/-
 Loss of Estate 15,000/-
Funeral Expenses 15,000/-

The learned tribunal has granted in-toto Rs.13,24,320/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum,
which the Insurance Company required to be deposited.
The enhanced amount would come to Rs.4,00,000/-, which the Insurance Company deposits within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order.
It is directed that the enhanced amount would be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till realization.
8. In the facts and circumstances, the present appeal is partly allowed, with no order as to costs.
The judgment and award dated 09.12.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Kheda at Nadiad in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1133 of 2018 shall stand modified as aforesaid.
